b: I’ve been waiting for this one for a long time.

Old Town has a new ePDL+ retroFit Kit that works across a bunch of different Old Town kayaks now. I first got to fish the ePDL+ drive from Old Town a few years ago on a trip to Maine. We were fishing from specific models that were purpose-built for the ePDL+ drive, such as the BigWater ePDL+ 132. And ever since then, I’ve been completely impressed by the drive because it fixes a classic problem: Many anglers want to switch from manual pedal power to electric power throughout the fishing day. And they want that all-in-one ability in their kayak, which many companies (including Old Town) offer by incorporating a trolling motor.

But a trolling motor definitely throws in a couple of variables! A trolling motor on a kayak almost always necessitates a trailer, and anglers out there like myself still like to throw a kayak into the back of our truck for transport. And that’s where the original ePDL+ drive really shined because it was super easy to remove and mount to an Old Town kayak in seconds.

The limiting factor was that only certain kayaks from Old Town could use the original ePDL+ drive. Recently, that’s dramatically changed as a new ePDL+ retroFit Kit allows anglers to use the drive in many different Old Town rigs. For anglers like me — and personally I have the Old Town Sportsman PDL 120 Pro — it’s been a blast to use this retrofit drive on my kayak for the past couple months.
Comparing the ePDL+ and PDL drives from Old Town.

So Old Town went and changed the whole game for folks who already had a PDL kayak sitting in their garage. If you’ve ever tried rigging an aftermarket trolling motor on a plastic boat, you already know the annoyance of drilling through your hull, snaking wires front to back, and wrestling a heavy battery into a tight spot. This new ePDL+ retroFit kit jumps past all that extra work. The entire drive setup — motor, controls, safety kill-switch, and battery — drops right down into the exact console well where your standard pedal drive normally sits. No drilling, no cut wires, and zero actions to void your hull’s warranty. For anybody running a Sportsman, Topwater, BigWater, or Salty out on the water, you can modernize your rig in about 30 seconds.

The different parts of this retro fit kit are simple. Old Town packed its power into a compact 36-volt, 6.5-amp-hour lithium battery that doesn’t weigh more than three pounds. It slips right into the top of the console and locks in place with a latched door; it’s where the kill switch is located, too. My kit also included a battery charger, plus the prop and hardware for the drive. It’s all easy to put together because a wrench and other tools are included. Extra parts I’d consider buying, especially if you’re a tournament angler or on the water a ton, include a spare prop kit and a second battery.

Don’t let the small size fool you. The new ePDL+ retroFit is a workhorse. When I compared it to my traditional PDL drive, the retrofit drive is much heavier (at about 35 pounds). So it is something to consider, although it has that same PDL handle that allows you to carry it to and from the water.

The way I used the new drive on full electric power was in the Cruise Control mode. On Cruise 1, it basically kept me in place hands-free when navigating against a light wind. It’s great for fishing in one spot against low wind or current. It also has a low power draw, and Old Town says you can get about 13 hours runtime out of it. Those cruise settings progress all the way up to Cruise 5. And that top setting, of course, has the largest power draw, and I was able to get up to a high speed of 4.5 mph. Running full bore will only give you about one hour run time, so don’t get too heavy handed or lazy with it.

But I’m not the type to go full electric all the time, or even most of the time. I really utilize the power-assist mode more than anything else with this drive. The exercise is always much needed for a guy who sits in an office chair way too much, and it just feels like pedaling an ebike in a slightly lower-to-earth position. Thirdly, you can pedal without any power assist or electric help — with the unit basically turned off in manual pedal mode — and it feels like a classic PDL drive.

The second you click on that Power Assist mode, it’s like catching a steady tailwind right when you need it most. And this unit does make clicking sounds, but they have a purpose to let you know when power assist or electric engages, so I learned to listen for those quiet click sounds. With five assist levels matching your pedal stroke, it does the heavy grunt work so your knees, calves, and hamstrings don’t pay the price. I realized whenever engaging the cruise mode or power assist mode, it’s worthwhile to first start pedaling to get the kayak moving. The interface on the drive just works better when you have a bit of a pedal going. But once cruise control was engaged, I could take my feet off the pedals and change speeds without any issues.

All in, you can put on the mileage pretty easily using power assist. And when you’re busy tying on a fresh jig or unhooking a ditch pickle, you just bump it back into cruise mode, pick your speed, and let the boat drive itself hands-free. The little LCD screen on the console stayed plenty bright to read through my polarized sunglasses, so you always know right where your battery level stands.

At $2,500, the new drive isn’t pocket change. But stacked up against buying a brand-new trolling motor and lithium battery (plus considering the extra rigging), upgrading your current Old Town rig makes a whole lot of sense. Old Town rolled this unit out in three different console sizes, meaning whether you’re in a 106, 120, or a BigWater 132, you have options.

So far, I’ve had a great time with the new Old Town ePDL+ retroFit Kit, and it has truly helped me in many different situations to flat-out catch more fish. Plus, I have outpaced a few storms back to the launch site.

Keep in mind, by motoring your kayak, your state might now require it to be registered at the DMV. And I did snag an error message every once in a while when using the drive, but it was almost always an operator error. For example, if I was trying to increase the power on pedal assist when not actually pedaling at all, then I got a warning.

Kayak fishing is supposed to be about unexplored waters and catching fish, not wearing out your legs or arms down while making that trek to your spot. This retroFit kit stretches your range, brings the power in a manageable package, keeps your hands on the rod where they belong, and gives that plastic hull you already trust a whole second lease on life. My older PDL drive is getting dusty in the garage as I use the new ePDL+ unit almost all the time now.
Drop-In Installation: Snaps directly into existing console with no wiring.
Three Propulsion Modes: Manual pedal, power-assisted pedal, or fully motorized cruise
Five Speed Settings: Adjusts up to 5 mph across five power levels
Integrated 36V Battery: Features a self-contained battery built directly into the unit
Safety Kill Switch: Cuts power automatically if you fall overboard
